can_fail_a.instructions: Can a bug in the behaviour this test names make the test fail?

criteria.true: yes: some bug in that behaviour fails it
criteria.false: no: it passes whatever the code does, as with a tautology, both sides from the code, or an assertion that never runs

can_fail_c.instructions: Would some wrong output of the behaviour this test names fail it?

criteria.true: yes: a wrong output fails it

asserts_content.instructions: Does an assertion compare the content of the output with an expected value?

criteria.true: yes: it checks what the output holds
criteria.false: no: only its type, length, keys, or truthiness, or nothing at all

asserts_own_value.instructions: Does the test write its expected value itself, as a literal or its own computation?

criteria.false: no: it comes from the code under test

asserts_shape_only.instructions: Do all assertions check only type, length, its list of keys, a bound, or truthiness?

criteria.false: no: an assertion checks a value

asserts_mock_only.instructions: Are all assertions about whether a mock or spy was called?

criteria.false: no: an assertion checks a result

asserts_input_only.instructions: Do the assertions only read the test's own variables, never a value the code under test returned?

criteria.true: yes: only its own input or setup
criteria.false: no: they read a value the code returned

positive_a.instructions: Does an assertion expect a non-empty value?

criteria.true: yes: a number, a string, true, an object, or an error message
criteria.false: no: only empty, null, undefined, or no throw

positive_b.instructions: Does this test check a real value, not only empty, null, or no throw?

criteria.true: yes: it checks a real value
criteria.false: no: only empty, null, undefined, or no throw

criteria.true: yes: no branch, loop, early return, or catch can skip or swallow one
criteria.false: no: a branch, a loop over a value that may be empty, an early return, or a catch can skip or swallow one

isolated.instructions: Does this test pass alone and in any order, reading nothing another test sets or changes?

criteria.true: yes: what it reads is built by it, a hook, or a fixture no test changes
criteria.false: no: it reads a value another test sets or changes

deterministic.instructions: Does this test give the same result on every run?

criteria.true: yes: nothing real-time, random, networked, or external, or it is faked
criteria.false: no: it uses the real clock, randomness, a sleep, the network, or an external file or env

automated.instructions: Does this test pass or fail with no person involved?

criteria.true: yes: no person must set up, act, or read

restores.instructions: Does this test leave all shared state as it found it?

criteria.true: yes: it changes none, or an after hook puts it back
criteria.false: no: it leaves a global, env variable, timer, mock, or shared object changed

resilient.instructions: Does this test reach and read the code only through its public interface?

criteria.true: yes: a public import, and it asserts a return, a throw, or an effect a caller sees
criteria.false: no: an internal import, a spy on a helper, a private or _ member, or a pinned internal call order
